source: Lohman, S.W., 1972, Ground-Water Hydraulics, USGS Professional Paper 708, Table 18 (p. 54) and Table 19 (p. 55), plus Fetter, C.W., 1988, Applied Hydrogeology (2nd ed.) example p. 165 as worked in Franke, Reilly, Buxton and Simmons, 1992, USGS Open-File Report 92-637, Part II - Instructor's Guide (p. 97)
unit: m of drawdown (inputs: m2/day, dimensionless, m3/day, m, days)
provider: U.S. Geological Survey (Professional Paper 708; Open-File Report 92-637)
license: USGS publications are in the public domain in the United States; quoted verbatim for non-commercial scientific validation with attribution - see tests/reference_data/theis_worked_example.md
valid_time: not applicable: synthetic worked examples, no calendar date stated in either source
spatial_reference: no location: hypothetical aquifers defined only by T and S
temporal_resolution: case row: one (r, t) pair per published case; t spans 1 to 1000 days
uncertainty: published drawdowns rounded by the sources: Lohman prints W(u) to 2 decimals and s to 3 significant figures, so each row carries <= 0.6 percent of published rounding; the test tolerance is +/- 2 percent
processing_history: v1 2026-10-10: values transcribed from the two primary-source PDFs fetched and read with pypdf; published feet converted to metres at 1 ft = 0.3048 m exactly; the Fetter/OFR row is already metric; no engine-derived values
